notes.title: 2026 Question Set 1: Choose the Correct Options
notes.content:
(1) India’s climate is of                 type. (March ’19; Sept. ’21)

(a) humid (b) monsoon (c) equatorial (d) cold

(2) Brazil gets rainfall from south-east and north-east winds.                                                (March ’22)

(a) monsoon (b) trade (eastern) (c) anti-trade (d) cyclonic

(3) In Brazil,                 receives orographic rainfall.

(a) Guyana Highlands

(b) windward side of the Great Escarpment

(c) Amazon river basin

(d) Paraguay – Parana river basin

(4) As the                  extent of Brazil is more, there is a variety in climatic conditions.

(a) equatorial             (b) latitudinal and longitudinal

(c) longitudinal           (d) latitudinal

(5) The Himalayas block the                       wind’s blowing from the north.                                            (March ’25)

(a) very cold (b) very hot (c) hot and dry (d) humid

Ans. (1) monsoon (2) trade (eastern) (3) windward side of the Great Escarpment (4) latitudinal (5) very cold.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 8: Identify the Incorrect Pair
notes.content:
Q. (a) Western Ghats – Region of low rainfall in India

(b) Drought Quadrilateral – Rain shadow region in Brazil

(c) Eastern Himalayas – Region of high rainfall in India

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 9: Answer in One Sentence
notes.content:
(1) What is rainshadow region in Brazil called?         (March ’22)

Ans. Rainshadow       region   in   Brazil   is   called   as    ‘Drought Quadrilateral’.

(2) Which type of climate is found to the south of the Tropic of Capricorn in Brazil?

Ans. Temperate type of climate is found to the south of the Tropic of Capricorn in Brazil.

(3) In which part of Brazil does less variations in temperature found?

Ans. Less variations in temperature is found in the equatorial region at coastal part in Brazil.

(4) What is the average rainfall in the Amazon river basin?

Ans. The average rainfall in the Amazon river basin is about 2000 mm.

(5) By which name is the northeast part of Brazil known?

Ans. The northeast part of Brazil is known as ‘Drought Quadrilateral’.

(6) Which form of rain is found in Himalayan region?

Ans. Orographic type of rain is found in Himalayan region.

notes.content:
(1) A type of rainfall that occurs again in Chennai and other southern regions of India.

(2) A type of rainfall that occurs in the equatorial region due to high temperature.

Ans. (1) Retreating monsoon         (2) Convectional rainfall.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 14: Write Short Notes
notes.content:
(13) Retreating monsoon.                             (March ’24)

Ans. (1) The southwest monsoon winds flowing from the mainland of India are obstructed by the Himalayan ranges in the north resulting their return journey backward towards the Indian Ocean.

(2) These winds blowing from northeast to southwest direction again brings monsoon to Indian Peninsula. This monsoon is called as retreating monsoon.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 17: Give Geographical Reasons
notes.content:
(8) India receives precipitation from the northeast monsoon winds too.                                 (Nov. ’20; March ’23)

Ans. (1) India receives most of its precipitation from the southwest monsoon winds. These winds enter the mainland of India from the southern regions and gradually flow towards the northern regions of India.

(2) These winds are obstructed by the Himalayan ranges in the north. As its effect, these winds start their return journey and start flowing backward towards the Indian Ocean.

(3) In their return journey, these winds blow from northeast to southwest direction. As its effect, these winds bring retreating monsoon in India. Thus, India receives precipitation from the northeast monsoon winds too.

(9) Snowfall doesn’t always occur in Brazil.            (Nov. ’20)

Ans. Snowfall generally occurs in temperate and polar regions due to polar winds, and in high-altitude mountains and hills. Brazil is not in the polar region; most of it lies in the tropics and it has no high mountain regions. Therefore snowfall does not generally occur in Brazil.

(10) Tropical cyclones occur rarely in Brazil. (July ’19 – ’22 – ’23; March ’24 – ’25)

Ans. (1) In the northern coastal region near equator, the differences in the temperatures are negligible.

(2) In this region, the winds move vertically.

(3) The convergence zone of the trade winds is also found to be weak in this region. Therefore, tropical cyclones occur rarely in Brazil.

(11) The northeastern part of Brazilian Highlands receives very less rainfall.                                         (July ’23)

Ans. (1) The winds blowing from the Southern Atlantic Ocean in the southeast and the northeast direction are obstructed by the Brazilian Highlands.

(2) These winds move upward along with the slopes of the Brazilian Highlands. At higher altitude, the condensation process takes place and windward side of Brazilian Highlands receives more rain.

(3) When these winds cross the top of Brazilian Highlands, go to other side of mountain, these winds are dry. As its effect, the leeward side of the Brazilian Highlands gets less rainfall. Therefore, the northeastern part of Brazilian Highlands receives very less rainfall.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 18: Draw a Graph and Answer the Questions
notes.content:
Q. 1. Observe the Figure (Graph) 4.4 given on page 27 of the textbook and answer the following questions :

(1) In which month is the highest temperature found in all the four cities?

Ans. In Manaus, the highest temperature is found in the months from August to October, in Belem it is found in the months of June to December, in Porto Alegre it is found in the months of January and February and in Rio de Janeiro it is found in the month of February.

(2) In which month does it rain the most in the given cities?

Ans. In Manaus, it rains most in the month of March, in Belem it is in the month of March, in Porto Alegre it is in the months of August and September and in Rio de Janeiro it is in the months of January and March.

(3) When does Brazil have its rainy season?

Ans. Brazil has its rainy season from September to November as well as from March to May.

(4) Which city has the maximum range of temperature? How much is it?

Ans. Manaus has the maximum range of temperature. It is nearly from 23°C (minimum temperature) to 33°C (maximum temperature).

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 20: Answer in Detail / Explain
notes.content:
(16) Explain the importance of Himalayas and the Indian Ocean with respect to the climate of India.               (Sept. ’21)

Ans. The importance of Himalayas and the Indian Ocean with respect to the climate of India can be explained as follows :

(1) The Indian Ocean and Himalayan ranges play an important role in formation of southeast monsoon winds.

(2) In summers, the temperature in Punjab Plains and the Thar desert is found to be high. As its effect, the areas of low pressure are developed.

(3) On the other hand, the areas of high pressure are found in the Indian Ocean. This leads to formation and flowing of southeast monsoon winds from the Indian Ocean to the mainland of India.

(4) These winds are moisture-laden and so they bring rainfall in India.

(5) Himalayas saves India by obstructing the passage of very cold winds from the north into India in winter.

(6) The southwest monsoon winds flow from the south to the north and reaches towards the Himalayas.

(7) These winds are obstructed by the Himalayas. Due to obstruction, these winds change their direction and start flowing from the northeast to the Indian Ocean.

(8) The return journey of these winds bring the retreating monsoon in peninsular region of India.

(17) Compare the climates of Brazil and India. (July ’19; March ’22)

Ans. The climates of Brazil and India can be compared with the help of the following points :

(1) Brazil’s climate is of tropical type. On the other hand, monsoon type of climate is seen in India.

(2) In Brazil, the temperature is comparatively higher in the northern part and lower in the southern part. On the other hand, in India, the temperature is comparatively lower in the northern part and higher in the southern part.

(3) In Brazil, the amount of rainfall is comparatively higher in the northern part and lower in the southern part. On the other hand, in India, the amount of rainfall is comparatively lower in the northern part and comparatively higher in the southern part.

(4) In Brazil, mild and humid climate is found near the coastal regions. On the other hand, in India, hot and humid climate is found near the coastal regions.

(18) Discuss the factors affecting climate of Brazil. (March ’19)

Ans. (1) Proximity to equator, Brazilian Highlands, the Great Escarpment are the main factors affecting climate of Brazil.

(2) Due to proximity to equator, the temperatures in the northern part of Brazil is comparatively higher. On the other hand, the temperatures in the southern part of Brazil is comparatively lower.

(3) The average temperature in the Amazon river basin in the northern part near equator is 25°C to 28°C. The overall climate in this region is found to be hot, humid and unhealthy.

(4) The amount of annual average rainfall in Amazon river valley is nearly 2000 mm. The amount of annual average rainfall is nearly 1000 mm to 1200 mm in the southeast coastal region.

(5) The temperature is comparatively low in the Brazilian highlands. Brazilian highlands receives moderate amount of rainfall, i.e. nearly 600 mm to 1200 mm.

(6) The great Escarpment and the Brazilian Highlands obstruct the trade winds blowing from the southeast and the northeast directions. This leads to heavy rainfall in the windward sides of the Great Escarpment, i.e. in the eastern coastal region of Brazil.

(7) The winds blowing beyond the Highlands become dry and therefore it rains less to the leeward side of the Great Escarpment and the Brazilian Highlands.

(8) As its effect, the northeast part of Brazil receives the minimum rainfall. The temperature is also found to be high in this region. This region is a rain shadow region. It is known as ‘Drought Quadrilateral’.

(19) Describe in brief the changes occurring in the climatic conditions of India while going from south to north.

Ans. The changes occurring in the climatic conditions of India while going from south to north are as follows :

(1) In India, as we go from south to north, the temperatures keep dropping.

(2) For example, in peninsular region located in the southern part of India, the average temperature is found to be ranging between 25°C and 30°C. On the other hand, mountainous regions located in the northern part of India, the average temperature is found to be ranging between 5°C and 10°C.

(3) In India, as we go from south to north, the amount of rainfall also keeps decreasing.

(4) For example, in Chennai (located in the southern part of India), the amount of the maximum average rainfall in the month of November is nearly 410 mm. On the other hand, in Delhi (located in the northern part of India), the amount of the maximum average rainfall in the month of August is nearly 250 mm.

(20) What could be the reasons behind the flowing of winds from different directions towards Brazil?

Ans. The following could be the reasons behind the flowing of winds from different directions towards Brazil :

(1) The equator passes through the northern part of Brazil. The low pressure belt is found near equatorial region in Brazil.

(2) The winds from high pressure belt from southern and northern hemisphere flow towards this region in Brazil.

(3) As its effect, in the northern part of Brazil, the northeast trade winds flow.

(4) Similarly, in the southern part of Brazil, the southeast trade winds flow.

(21) Correlate northeast and southeast trade winds and rainfall with reference to obstruction in their way.

Ans. (1) The Great Escarpment and the Brazilian Highlands obstructs the northeast and southeast trade winds.

(2) As its effect, these winds move upwards along the slopes of the Great Escarpment and the Brazilian Highlands.

(3) At higher altitude, the condensation process takes place and windward side receives more rain.

(4) Thus, the windward side of the Great Escarpment and the Brazilian Highlands receive abundant rainfall and the rain shadow region is found to the other side.

(22) Give information about Drought Quadrilateral in Brazil.

Ans. (1) The Great Escarpment and the Brazilian Highlands obstructs the trade winds flowing in southeast and northeast from the Atlantic Ocean.

(2) Due to this obstruction, it rains heavily in the windward side of the Great Escarpment and the Brazilian Highlands, i.e. in the eastern coastal region of Brazil.

(3) The amount of annual average rainfall in the eastern coastal region of Brazil is nearly 1200 mm.

(4) The winds that reach the top of the Great Escarpment and the Brazilian Highlands become dry. The capacity of holding moisture of these winds increases.

(5) As its effect it rains less to the leeward side of the Great Escarpment and the Brazilian Highlands.

(6) Thus, the northeast part of Brazil receives the minimum rainfall.

(7) The amount of annual average rainfall is only nearly 600 mm in this region. This region is a rain shadow region.

(8) It is known as ‘Drought Quadrilateral’. The higher temperature is found in this region.

notes.title: July 2024 Solved Paper, Assignment and July 2025 Practice Paper
notes.content:
July 2024 Board Paper — Q.2(2): Identify the wrong pair: India’s climate—monsoon; north Brazil—Equator; centre of India—Tropic of Capricorn; east Brazil—Atlantic Ocean.

Ans. Centre of India—Tropic of Capricorn is the wrong pair.

Q.3(3): Write a short note on the importance of the Indian Ocean.

Ans. The Indian Ocean helps form the southwest monsoon. In summer, heating over the Punjab Plains and Thar Desert creates low pressure, while higher pressure over the Indian Ocean draws moisture-laden winds toward India. These winds bring rainfall.

Assignment — Differentiate between the climates of India and Brazil. Q.5(1): Give a geographical reason why there is little range of temperature in Manaus.

Assignment answers are not printed in the supplied PDF; it refers to a separate Geography Digest.

July 2025 Practice Board Paper — Q.1(2): What type of climate is found in northern Brazil? Options: monsoon, hot, cold, temperate. Q.7(2): Explain the importance of the Himalayas and the Indian Ocean with respect to India’s climate.

The July 2025 answers are not printed in the supplied PDF; it points to a QR code for model answers.

What is the main reason Brazil's climate is varied?
flashcards.back: Its large latitudinal extent (from near the Equator to the Tropic of Capricorn).
A rainshadow region in the northeastern part of Brazil that receives very low rainfall.

flashcards.front: What are the two main trade winds that influence Brazil's climate?

quiz.question: India's climate is of which type?
quiz.explanation: India is characterized by its monsoon type of climate, with a distinct seasonal reversal of winds.

quiz.question: Brazil gets rainfall from which winds?
quiz.explanation: Brazil receives rainfall primarily from the southeast and northeast trade winds, which originate from the Atlantic Ocean.

quiz.question: In Brazil, which region receives orographic rainfall?
options: Windward side of the Great Escarpment
quiz.explanation: The windward side of the Great Escarpment receives heavy orographic rainfall as the moist trade winds are forced to rise.

quiz.question: Tropical cyclones occur rarely in Brazil because:
options: It is located near the equator.
The Atlantic Ocean is too cold.
The trade winds are too weak.
quiz.explanation: Near the equator, the temperature differences are negligible, and the trade wind convergence is weak, conditions that are not conducive for tropical cyclone formation.
